answer: One driver, one licence: the national licensing authority signs each epoch challenge binding the agent's key to a single driving licence, re-checked against the authority register every epoch. A second key claiming the same licence is rejected outright, since the authority, not the claimant, holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 real licences at roughly $2,500 each in lessons and tests, about $2,500,000, plus a bridge of logged driving hours no script can fake — and any licence can be revoked on fraud, a signal no attacker can dodge, leaving a haven of dead credentials.
